newsitem.title: GERMANY: German group sees north-south split in WTO.
newsitem.headline: German group sees north-south split in WTO.

text.p: A German retailing group on Friday welcomed the results of the World Trade Organisation's (WTO) ministers conference, but said more must be done to avert conflict between rich and poor nations.
"More liberalisation incentives are needed to avert the danger of a North-South conflict within the WTO," the Cologne-based Trade Association of German Retailers said.
The group said the WTO more than met its modest expectations for the conference.
But it regretted that so little action was taken in the clothing and textiles sector, important to many developing countries.
The conference's focus on information technology reflected the interest of industrialised countries, and hampered European Commission efforts for broader tariff reductions.

Steps to improve market access for all would help integrate poorer countries in the world trade system, it said. The group welcomed European efforts to admit China and other countries in the WTO despite opposition from the U.S.
Ingomar Hauchler, parliamentary spokesman on the world economy for the opposition Social Democrats, said the WTO agreement was a poor compromise that fell far short of expectations.
"This is a tragic result, as it allows the continuance of the common practices of repression of unions, and the forcing of 250 million children worldwide to work under exploitative conditions."
But Hauchler saw a positive side in the creation of working groups to develop rules for international competition and international investment.
